memoryText: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Matthew 28:19-20 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These are the last words of Matthew’s Gospel, spoken by the risen Lord. They sum up what the church exists to do and the promise that makes it possible.

“Go therefore.” The “therefore” connects to the claim in the previous verse: all authority belongs to Jesus. Because he is Lord of all, we go. The mission rests on his authority and not on our ability.

“And make disciples of all nations.” The main command is to make disciples, followers and learners of Jesus. “Go,” “baptize,” and “teach” all serve this. And it is for all nations, every people and language. The blessing promised to Abraham now goes out to the world.

“Baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” New disciples are brought into the community of the triune God and his people.

“Teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you.” Discipleship is about obedience and not just information. It takes time, and it includes the whole of Jesus’ teaching, including the Sermon on the Mount.

“And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” The promise is the secret to all of it. We are not sent alone. The one with all authority is with us in every place and every year until he comes. “Behold” tells us to look at this and take courage.

You may not be going to another country, but you are called to make disciples where you are: at home, work, school, and church. Say this verse as a commission and as a comfort.
weekInReview: This week you walked through the last days of Jesus’ ministry in Matthew. You saw him teach about marriage, wealth, and servant leadership, and give his life as a ransom for many. You watched the king enter Jerusalem on a donkey, answer his enemies with parables and wisdom, and give the two great commandments. In the Olivet Discourse, he called you to be ready and faithful until he returns. In Psalm 118, you read the song of the rejected stone. You sat at the Last Supper, heard the words of the new covenant, and watched him pray in Gethsemane. You followed him through the trials, the mockery, and the cross, and you stood at the empty tomb to hear the Great Commission. Two doctrinal days gave you the Trinity and baptism. Together, they show that the King has come, died, and risen, and that he sends his people to the nations with his presence.
reflectionQuestions: The Great Commission says to make disciples of all nations. Who is one person in your life that you could invest in as a disciple, or from whom you could learn as a disciple?
Jesus promises, “I am with you always.” In what situation do you most need to believe that promise right now?
Matthew began with Immanuel, “God with us,” and ended with “I am with you always.” How does that frame change the way you read the whole Gospel?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that all authority is his and he is with you always.
Ask him to send you to make disciples where you are.
Tell him who you will begin with.
